ten_goi.chu: Still, many well-known mythologies feature moon goddesses, including the Greek goddess Selene, the Roman goddess Luna, the Chinese goddess Chang'e, and the Aztec goddess Coyolxāuhqui, whose decapitation may represent a lunar eclipse.

moc.chu: She drives her moon chariot across the heavens.
Selene is best known for her affair with the beautiful mortal Endymion.
She found Endymion so beautiful that she asked her cousin, Zeus, to grant him eternal youth so that he would never leave her.
Whatever the case, Zeus granted Selene's wish and put Endymion into an eternal sleep.
Theocritus portrays Endymion's sleep as enviable because (presumably) of Selene's love for him.
The Roman playwright Seneca, has Selene abandoned the night sky for Endymion's sake having entrusted her "shining" moon chariot to her brother Helios to drive.
